grid: For Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2000 collection, Tom Ford paired pared-back silhouettes with punk references. The exposed pin engraved with the Gucci logo echoes that contrast on this straight-cut denim wrap skirt, which was originally sold with the pin as its fastening.
The show report establishes Ford’s punk reference. The comparable wrap skirt has the original pin; the photographed skirt is missing its pin. No exact runway claim.

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana drew on Sicilian imagery for Spring/Summer 2013. They put the same Taormina print on a sleeveless dress shown on the runway.
The sleeveless dress was on the runway. The short-sleeve top shares its print and is not identified as a runway piece.

Yohji Yamamoto used folds and uneven cuts to shape black skirts as early as Spring/Summer 1993. In his notes for that collection, he described working with folded fabric and curving cuts. On this skirt, layered pleated panels bring the fabric down to an uneven hem.
Yamamoto’s own notes document the earlier fold-and-cut method. The date of this skirt is unconfirmed.

{"history_links":[{"title":"Powerhouse Museum and Yamamoto’s collection notes","url":"https://collection.powerhouse.com.au/object/384528","kind":"Museum, house or primary record"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Boutique listing","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/products/14-06-2026_yohji-yamamoto_49","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}

For Fall/Winter 1998, Jean Paul Gaultier printed cathedral architecture and stained-glass motifs onto stretch mesh. A hooded top from the same season uses the same imagery. On this crewneck, the print runs across the body and down the sleeves.
The comparison is a hooded version of the cathedral print, not this crewneck on the runway.

Jean Paul Gaultier broke a portrait into concentric bands for Fall/Winter 2001. A snap-front mesh top from the season carried the print in colour. On this top, the portrait appears in black and grey across the back.
The snap-front top is a comparison for the portrait treatment. It is not the item being sold.

Alexander Calder’s mobiles inspired the suspended shapes in Jean Paul Gaultier’s Spring/Summer 2003 collection. One runway look paired a top hung with geometric pieces with gathered pink trousers. This peach pair uses similar gathering at the knees above flared hems.
The show source establishes the Calder reference and a related gathered-leg design. The peach pair is not asserted to be the runway garment.

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana carried the crumpled finish of their previous womenswear collection into their Spring/Summer 2008 menswear show, where they used it on combat-inspired pieces. Look 24 paired this cargo-short design with a crinkled jacket.
Look 24 is cited as the cargo-short design match. The listing documents the sale example.

Tom Ford worked fur into black knitwear for Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2002 collection. Liisa Winkler wore this skirt design under a satin coat in look 22, with its vertical fur strips and looped hem visible beneath it.
Look 22 is cited as the skirt design match. This does not establish runway provenance of the sale garment.

Maison Martin Margiela took inspiration from the gesture of pulling a coat collar over the head to shelter from rain. On this cardigan, the extended collar drapes across the shoulders and becomes a hood when pulled up.
Read the house’s original description of the rain-sheltering gesture on printed p. 280 of the thesis, alongside the item’s documented collar construction.

Tom Ford shaped Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2003 outerwear around a cinched waist, opening the show with a white coat fastened by a broad corset belt. Curved topstitched seams bring that waist shaping into this shorter cotton jacket.

Roberto Cavalli drew on Chinese dress and ornament for Spring/Summer 2003, reworking the cheongsam as a fitted satin minidress. Eva Herzigová wore a silk dress with a version of this T-shirt’s floral print at the Milan show.
Herzigová wore a different garment with a version of the floral print. The interview documents the cheongsam reference, not the origin of the motif.

Jean Paul Gaultier experimented with prints that traced the body in the mid-1990s. A jacket from his 1996 ‘Cyberbaba’ collection mapped a nude figure in dots. On this JPG Jean’s shirt, curved stripes trace the torso across the front and back.
The museum piece documents the earlier body-mapping approach. It does not date this shirt to Spring/Summer 1996.

Alexander McQueen used layers of sheer black fabric in his 2008 eveningwear. A strapless dress from Fall/Winter 2008 in LACMA’s collection layers strips of silk crepe through the skirt. On this cap-sleeve dress, a single layer of mesh extends below the opaque lining.
The museum’s Fall/Winter piece is a different, strapless dress. This label supports 2008 only; no collection or runway match is established.

{"history_links":[{"title":"LACMA’s related 2008 dress","url":"https://collections.lacma.org/object/274479","kind":"Related design"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Exact boutique listing and label photos","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/collections/alexander-mcqueen/products/26-07-2025_alexander-mcqueen_41","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}

Around 2001, Tom Ford used ties in place of buttons on Gucci tailoring. A silk faille jacket from the period in LACMA’s collection fastens with narrow ties. This cropped blazer closes with a broad sash knotted at the waist.
The museum ensemble shows a tied Gucci jacket from about 2001. It is not this ivory blazer; the item’s specific season is unconfirmed.

Maison Martin Margiela carried the high waist of Spring/Summer 2007 into the following winter collection. On the runway, look 29 paired a similar high-waisted cut with sharply squared shoulders.
The house notes support the high waist. Runway look 29 is a comparison for the cut, not a claim about this sale item.

{"history_links":[{"title":"Runway look 29, related high-waisted trousers","url":"https://nowfashion.com/media/maison-margiela-ready-to-wear-fall-winter-2007-paris-fashion-week-runway-029","kind":"Related design"},{"title":"Original show notes, p. 289","url":"https://scriptiebank.be/file/17538/download?token=BOJz9Eni#page=297","kind":"Museum, house or primary record"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Boutique listing","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/products/31-07-2026_maison-margiela_61","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}

Dirk Bikkembergs drew on military, mountaineering and work boots for his early footwear. On this 1990s pair, the laces pass through the heel and wrap around the shaft, a fastening that recalls climbing boots.
Beige Crystal Fishnet Tank Top Set

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana paired mesh and crystals on bras they showed as tops for Spring/Summer 2000, a combination they returned to on the fishnet tank. Jennifer Lopez wore a version in her 2002 video for ‘Jenny from the Block’, styled by Andrea Lieberman.
The video shows a version of the design. Spring 2000 supplies a material precedent; differing early-2000s dates for the set do not establish a specific season.

Blue Denim Maxi Skirt with Gold Sequins

Roberto Cavalli began embellishing jeans with leather patchwork in the 1970s. He returned to denim for Spring/Summer 2001, using gold-tone sequins to draw radiating lines across the long skirt shown on the runway.
Original runway image supports the skirt design; house history supplies the earlier denim precedent.

Rei Kawakubo launched Comme des Garçons Girl in Spring/Summer 2015 with rounded collars and separates drawn from school uniforms. This jacket keeps the rounded collar and places oversized fabric knots diagonally across the front.
The retailer style number helps identify this jacket. Line debut coverage supports the school-uniform reference, not that this later jacket was at the debut.

Ann Demeulemeester worked with military dress and leather outerwear in the 2000s, pairing fitted biker jackets with jodhpurs on her Fall/Winter 2004 runway. This jacket uses an aviator cut, with shoulder tabs and an off-centre fastening.

Tom Ford pared back the ornament for Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2001 collection and ran metal zips down the front of runway trousers in the place of tuxedo stripes. On this leather pair, the zips extend the full length of both legs.

Jean Paul Gaultier reproduced Pierre-Auguste Cot’s 1880 painting ‘The Storm’ in the medallion on the back of this Maille Femme cardigan. He showed the same image facing forward on an openwork knit in his Fall/Winter 2007 collection, which drew on dress from the Scottish Highlands.
The Met identifies Cot’s source painting, and runway look 45 shows the motif facing forward on a knit. Gaultier’s specific reason for choosing the painting is unconfirmed.

Helmut Lang reworked the motorcycle jacket for Spring/Summer 2004. One version used cotton and cut-outs to lighten the heavy protective original. This leather version keeps the angled zip and broad lapels, with lace-up sides that release long ties below the hem.
The FIT label documents a related cut-out cotton biker jacket. The sale item is a different leather version.

{"history_links":[{"title":"Museum at FIT exhibition label","url":"https://exhibitions.fitnyc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/Beyond_Rebellion_Biker_Jacket_labels.pdf#page=19","kind":"Museum, house or primary record"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Boutique listing","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/products/09-10-2026_helmut-lang_32","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}

Martin Margiela began Artisanal in 1989 with a vest assembled from found porcelain shards. For Fall/Winter 2002, the house used reconstruction in its tailoring, joining matte upper panels to lustrous fabric on the lower legs of these trousers.
Blue and Yellow Orbital Print Top and Skirt Set
Issey Miyake developed a method of pleating clothes after they were cut and sewn. On this set, the orbital print runs across the narrow pleats of both the top and skirt.

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana drew on Napoleonic dress for Fall/Winter 2006, opening the show with a tableau of hussars and Empire gowns. They cut military tailcoats in shearling, carrying the uniform reference into plush collars and rows of metal buttons like those on this coat.
The runway review supports the Napoleonic reference and shearling at collection level.

Black Flared Trousers with Denim Panels

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana cut up and reassembled denim for Spring/Summer 2001, sending out distressed jeans held together with safety pins. Another runway look used a shaped denim yoke with black flared legs, the construction seen on this pair.
The seller’s comparison connects the shaped denim yoke and black flares to a runway design. It does not establish provenance of this individual pair.

Nicolas Ghesquière studied Cristóbal Balenciaga’s archive for Fall/Winter 2006, revisiting the founder’s moulded tailoring. A belted version of this sculpted-shoulder shape appeared on the runway over narrow trousers.
Ghesquière’s archive study is the collection context. The runway example is a belted version of the shape.

Rei Kawakubo reworked Victorian and Edwardian tailoring for ‘Dark Romance, Witch’, her Fall/Winter 2004 collection for Comme des Garçons. The top she showed at the Lido in Paris pairs a sheer bodice with one tailored sleeve and a feathered shoulder.
Look 17 supplies the one-sleeve and feathered-shoulder design comparison; styling on the runway need not be included with the sale top.

Paco Rabanne used slit openings to break up fitted outerwear for Fall/Winter 2000. A white coat in the show opened at the shoulders. This leather jacket carries the cut-outs across the chest and behind the elbows as well.
The related runway design is a white coat with slits. The sale jacket is black leather and is not the same piece.

Martin Margiela first enlarged clothes from dolls’ wardrobes to human scale for Fall/Winter 1994, keeping the original proportions and small construction details. The label inside these trousers identifies them as a reproduction of a doll’s garment.
The Met explains the Doll’s Wardrobe project. The label on these trousers identifies the doll-garment reproduction.

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana used long fringe to interrupt the outline of their Fall/Winter 1993 eveningwear. On one surviving ensemble it hangs from a lace shawl. On this runway design, the fringe falls in tiers from the dress itself.
LACMA’s dress-and-shawl ensemble documents fringe in the collection; the boutique’s runway comparison is separate evidence for the tiered dress design.

Phoebe Philo introduced the Luggage in 2010, adapting a Céline suitcase design from the 1970s. Daria Werbowy and Stella Tennant carried the Luggage in the house’s Spring/Summer 2011 campaign, photographed by Juergen Teller.
The evidence is about the Luggage family and the 2011 campaign. It does not claim the sale bag itself appeared in the campaign.

For Yves Saint Laurent’s Fall/Winter 2002 collection, Tom Ford developed the fuller upper-body proportions he had introduced at Gucci. On this jacket, overlapping suede panels build volume across the shoulders and chest.

{"history_links":[{"title":"R35 Yves Saint Laurent runway","url":"https://www.vogue.com/fashion-shows/fall-2002-ready-to-wear/saint-laurent","kind":"Runway or archive reference"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Boutique listing","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/products/12-05-2026_saint-laurent_56","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}
Black Wool Jacket with Detachable Mink Collar

Tom Ford revisited a tied-waist coat from 1999 in his final Gucci show, adding a fur collar to the new version. This black wool jacket appeared in the same Fall/Winter 2004 show with its own raised fur collar and low waist tie.
Ford’s earlier tied coat and this 2004 design are distinct. Keep the 1999 and 2004 references separate.

Jean Paul Gaultier traced his corset designs to a salmon-pink girdle he found in his grandmother Marie Garrabé’s wardrobe. The Spring/Summer 1989 runway showed a peach version of this strappy corset shape, with the lingerie construction worn in view.
The Galliera entry is a source for Gaultier’s corsetry precedent. The peach runway version is a comparison, not a claim about this black item.

Brown Silk Chiffon Dress with Slip

Jean Paul Gaultier used corset construction to shape printed silk chiffon in Spring/Summer 2004. A dress from that collection combines a corseted back with an asymmetric cut. This dress uses lacing at the back and lets the chiffon fall to an uneven hem.
Artcurial documents a different corseted chiffon dress from Spring/Summer 2004. The listing shows a separate slip included with row 38.

For Fall/Winter 1999, Maison Martin Margiela painted over vintage menswear for its Artisanal line. On this blazer, the silver coating has cracked across the surface, with the original dark cloth visible beneath the lapels.

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana brought lingerie onto the Spring/Summer 1991 runway, showing sequinned bra tops and bustiers alongside chiffon tunics. This red top carries the shaped cups into a square-necked bodice with gathered shoulders and long sleeves.

{"history_links":[{"title":"Original runway footage","url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XjFr74jZHBE","kind":"Runway or archive reference"},{"title":"Contemporary Los Angeles Times runway coverage","url":"https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-10-12-vw-2077-story.html","kind":"Runway or archive reference"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Boutique listing","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/products/14-03-2025_dolce-gabbana_11","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}

Tom Ford worked strips of fur into the seams of black knitwear for Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2002 collection. On this cardigan, those strips run across the body and sleeves, with long ends hanging past the hem.

{"history_links":[{"title":"Gucci Fall/Winter 2002 review","url":"https://www.vogue.com/fashion-shows/fall-2002-ready-to-wear/gucci","kind":"Editorial or interview"},{"title":"LACMA, related fur knit","url":"https://collections.lacma.org/object/226272","kind":"Related design"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Boutique listing","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/products/23-04-2026_gucci_37","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}

Martin Margiela had vintage garments photographed for Spring/Summer 1996, then transferred the images onto flat fabric. This cardigan reproduces a Shetland coat, with its lapels, buttons and back waist detail printed onto the jersey.

For Spring/Summer 2005, the Margiela atelier cut up older dresses and reassembled them for its Artisanal line. On this dress, contrasting prints and sheer fabrics meet in panels that fall to different lengths.
Black Nylon Chocolate Bar Shoulder Bag

Chanel used square quilting on its early-2000s Chocolate Bar bags in materials including tweed and calfskin. This nylon version carries the same grid into a flap bag with a chain strap and interlocking CC turn-lock.

{"history_links":[{"title":"R44 and R48 Chanel square-quilted comparison","url":"https://www.sothebys.com/en/buy/pdp/fashion/handbag/crossbody/_chanel-white-orange-tweed-single-flap-shoulder-bag-2000-6091","kind":"Related design"}],"item_links":[{"title":"Boutique listing","url":"https://elevated-archives.com/products/04-09-2026_chanel_47","kind":"Exact item evidence"}]}

Dark Olive Belted Leather Field Jacket

Trussardi began as a leather glove maker in 1911 and later applied its leatherworking to ready-to-wear under Nicola Trussardi. This jacket uses leather for a field-jacket cut, with a buckle belt and oversized flap pockets.
Thierry Hermès opened a harness-making workshop in Paris in 1837. The straps and buckles printed inside the waistband and at the turned-up cuffs echo the horse tack made by the house.
The house documents its harness-making origin. The prints are a design echo, not a confirmed motif commission or collection date.
